title: Quarterly Tranche Plan: Private/VPC Enterprise Signals & OKR Mapping
creator: Aisha M. Patel
description:
Summary: This ticket captures the end-to-end quarterly tranche plan for Private/VPC/on‑prem enterprise features targeted for the upcoming quarter. Goal is to deliver a small, high-confidence set of capabilities (RBAC, audit logging, upgrade compatibility, and a cost/latency dashboard) as Tranche 1, aligned to OKR: Increase Private deployment adoption by enterprise customers by 25% while maintaining 99.9% uptime for dedicated capacity.

Scope: Tranche 1 (priority):
- RBAC primitives for tenant and team scoping in Private control plane
- Audit logging export (structured, KMS-backed) and searchability in Console
- Upgrade compatibility gates and a runbook for 1→2 minor releases
- Console route-level cost + latency signal surface for Private customers

Out of scope for this tranche: full SSO multi-idp flows, on-prem offline installer (future tranche), dedicated autoscaling policy editor (follow-on).

Success metrics / OKR signals:
- OKR alignment: Private adoption +25% (activation within 90 days for pilot cohort)
- Telemetry: error rate <0.5% 95p, median token latency within SLA, and per-route cost delta reported within 5% of backend accounting
- Operational: Upgrade rollback rate <1% for canary cohorts, full E2E tests in CI for RBAC paths

Trade-offs considered:
- Fast shipping smaller feature set vs. surface completeness. Chosen approach: ship composable RBAC primitives now to unblock regulated customers, delay advanced RBAC policies to next tranche to limit blast radius.
- Strong telemetry vs. implementation time: initially expose summarized per-route metrics; richer attribution will be captured in telemetry backlog.

Rollout plan (waves):
- Dark launch: internal + opt-in beta customers (2 customers) for 2 weeks to validate telemetry and API ergonomics.
- Canary: 10 pilot customers with staged traffic (10%, 50%, 100%) per customer with automatic rollback triggers.
- General availability: GA after canary metrics meet gates for 14 days.

Gating metrics for canary -> GA:
- SLO: 99.9% availability for control plane operations affecting Private clusters
- Stability: no critical upgrade failures; rollback triggers if >0.5% requests error for 30m window
- Observability: console shows route-level cost/latency for pilot customers and alerts are wired to oncall

Artifacts & links:
- PRD: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1bPrd-private-tranche-1-prd
- Confluence runbook draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PD/pages/Private+Tranche+1+Runbook
- GitHub epic: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deployments/epics/274999
- Monitoring dashboard (staging): https://dashboards.redwood.internal/d/private-tranche-1-staging
- Incident learnings (upgrade regression): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1UpgradePostmortem

Notes for stakeholders: prioritize coordination with Security (KMS) and Infra (kernel/quantization compatibility) early; expect two design reviews and one security gating session prior to canary.
acceptance_criteria: RBAC: API + Console flows implemented and E2E-tested for tenant/team scoping
Audit logging: KMS-backed export enabled; logs searchable in Console for pilot customers
Upgrade gates: automated preflight + rollback hooks documented and exercised in staging
Console telemetry: per-route cost and latency tiles visible for pilot customers and linked to alerts
Load validation: canary load test shows throughput >= expected baseline and error rate below thresholds
Docs: PRD -> final, runbook -> published, customer-facing release notes drafted
